Synopsis:
Princeton economist Markus Brunnermeier presented at the Kansas City Fed's Jackson Hole symposium warning of severe AI-driven disruption to financial markets and central bank effectiveness. Key risks include AI agents achieving "asymmetric understanding" of Fed policy — anticipating actions before policymakers themselves — enabling market gaming at scale. Proposed mitigations (dual press conferences, opacity in communication) are framed as partial at best. Fed Chair Warsh struck a more optimistic tone on AI productivity. Conference also addressed stablecoins and DLT. Overall mood: cautious acknowledgment of risk, no concrete policy response yet.
